title: Arrumando a mochila
grammar: My e your para dizer de quem é
reading: I pack my bag for class.
My backpack is on the desk.
My notebook is in the backpack.
My pencil and my pen are in the bag.
My sister is here, and my brother is here too.
My name is on my notebook.
dialogue: Excuse me, Tom. Is this your backpack on the desk?
Yes, it is. Thank you! My notebook is in it.
And is this your pencil? It is on the floor.
No, it isn't. My pencil is in my bag.
I see. My name is Lia. This is my sister, Mia.
Nice to meet you, Lia. Is Mia a friend from school?
Yes, she is. She is my sister and my friend too.
Great! Thank you for the help, Lia.

title: Comprando uma passagem só de ida
reading: Ben is at the train station today.
He is at the ticket counter with a coffee.
The backpack is on the floor.
A one-way ticket is ten dollars.
The train is at nine in the morning.
Ben is tired, but he is happy.
dialogue: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes. Can I have one ticket to Boston, please?
Sure. One-way or round trip?
One-way, please. Is the train at nine?
Yes, it is. A ticket is twenty dollars.
Okay. Here is the money. I am tired today.
Here you are. Is this your backpack on the floor?
Yes, it is. Thank you! I am happy today.

title: Conferindo o bilhete impresso
grammar: This e these ao mostrar itens próximos
reading: Emma is at the train station with a coffee to go.
These are two printed tickets.
This ticket is for today.
The other ticket is for tomorrow.
The seat number is three.
Both tickets are in the small pocket.
dialogue: Good morning. Are these your tickets?
Yes, they are. Can I check the date with you?
Sure. This ticket is for today, and the other is for tomorrow.
Great. Is the seat number on the ticket?
Yes, it is. Look at this small number.
I see it. Are both tickets one-way?
Yes, both are one-way. Here are your tickets.
Perfect. Two tickets are in my pocket. Thank you!

title: A espera na biblioteca
grammar: There is para apontar um lugar disponível
reading: I am Tom, and I am at the library.
A quiet reading room is on the first floor.
A big table is by the window.
There is one seat at the table.
I have a book and a glass of water.
Now I can read in the quiet room.
dialogue: Excuse me, I have a quick question about the library.
Sure. Is it about a book?
No. I would like a quiet seat to read.
There is a seat at the big table.
Really? Is the table in the reading room?
Yes, it is. There is a window there too.
Great. Can I take my glass of water?
Yes, you can. Please have a seat.

title: Perguntando sobre um parque
grammar: Is there…? para perguntar se existe um lugar
reading: Today is my birthday, and I am in a new town.
I would like a small party in a park.
There is a park near here, on a quiet street.
There is a green gate at the entrance.
The gate is not far, so I go there with my dog.
Now I sit at my party with some water.
dialogue: Excuse me, is there a park near here?
Yes, there is. It is on Green Street.
Is it far? I have my dog with me.
No, it isn't. It is a quick walk.
Great. Is there an entrance on this street?
Yes, there is a green gate on the corner.
Thank you. Today is my birthday, so I have a party there.
Happy birthday! Yes, you can have a party there.

title: Onde eu moro
grammar: In, near e on para situar a moradia
reading: My name is Lia, and I live in a small town.
I live near the sea, in a quiet neighborhood.
My house is on Oak Street.
My mother and father live in the house with me.
There is a park near my house.
On Saturday, I sit in the park and see the sea.
dialogue: Hi Lia. Where is your house?
It is on Oak Street, in a small town.
Nice. Is your neighborhood near the sea?
Yes, it is. I live near the sea and a park.
Really? Is there a place to sit near your house?
Yes, there is. My mother and father are in the park on Saturday.
Great. Can I sit with you on Saturday?
Sure, you can. I am at the park gate on Saturday.

title: À beira do lago
grammar: Next to, by e across from para indicar posição
reading: I am Sam, and Jo is my sister.
We are in the park, by a pond.
The path is next to the pond.
There is a bench by the water, across from a tree.
My brother is on the path, near the sign.
We take a seat on the bench, and it is quiet.
dialogue: Sam, where is the path to the gate?
It is next to the pond, near the entrance.
Is there a bench near the pond?
Yes, there is. It is across from the big tree.
Nice. And where is Tom? Is he near the sign?
No, he is with the duck at the pond.
Great. Is the bench free for me and Tom?
Yes, it is. We can sit on the bench by the water.

title: Escolhendo o lugar de sentar
grammar: A pergunta Where can I sit?
reading: My family and I are at a small restaurant on Main Street.
I would like a window seat, please.
There is an empty table by the window.
A server is at the door, and I ask, 'Where can I sit?'
The restaurant is quiet, and there is a menu on the table.
I take a chair, and my family and I sit.
dialogue: Hi. Where can I sit with my family?
You can sit at the empty table by the door.
Can I have a window seat, please?
Sure. This table is by the window. Here you are.
Thank you. Where can I put my bag?
You can put it on the chair next to you.
Great. Can I have the menu and some water?
Yes, of course. Here is a menu and a glass of water.

title: Escrevendo o nome no papel
reading: I am Rosa, and I am on a chair at my desk.
There is a sheet of paper on my desk.
I have a blue pen and a name tag.
The teacher is nice: Write your name, please.
I write my name on the line at the top of the page.
Then I put the paper on the empty table.
dialogue: Excuse me, where can I sit and write my name?
Write your name at the top of the page, please.
Can I use my blue pen for the name?
Yes, you can. The blue pen is good.
Can I write my last name too?
Yes. Write both names on the line, please.
Great. Can I put the paper on the empty table?
Yes, you can. Put it there, please.

title: Uma instrução de segurança no trajeto
reading: My friends and I walk on a trail.
There is a sign near a bridge.
The sign is red and big: Stay on the path.
The bridge is wet, so we do not run.
We are happy, but we are tired.
We take a seat on a bench by the water.
dialogue: Can we run across the bridge, Mia?
No. Do not run on the wet bridge.
Okay. Can we leave the trail here?
No. Stay on the path, please.
Is there a sign by the fence?
Yes, there is. Do not go near the fence.
Okay. I am tired, but I am happy.
Me too. We can sit on a bench by the water.

title: Descrevendo a cidade à beira-mar
reading: I am Alex, and I am in a small seaside town.
The town is on the coast, near a big beach.
The street is quiet in the morning.
I see white houses and a small café.
There is a café with a coastal view.
I am hungry, so I take a chair at the café.
dialogue: What kind of place is this, Alex?
It is a small seaside town on the coast.
Is the street busy, or is it quiet?
It is quiet. There are white houses on the street.
Nice. I am hungry. Is there a café near here?
Yes, there is a café with a coastal view.
Great. Can we sit at a table near the path?
Yes, we can. I see an empty table there, and it is free.

title: Marcando a saída do trem
reading: Ana is at the station.
There is a small departure board on the wall.
The schedule is on the board.
There are three trains this morning.
The old train is at seven.
Ana is on time.
dialogue: Excuse me, where is the departure board for Boston?
It is over there. Go straight, then turn left at the sign.
Thank you. Is there a train to Boston this morning?
Yes, there is. Do not leave your bag here, and look at the schedule.
I see three trains. Is the first one on time?
Yes, it is. The first train is at seven.
Great! Is there another train for the afternoon?
Yes, there is one train at three.

title: Escolhendo uma hora para se encontrar
grammar: What time para pedir um horário
reading: Zoe is at the bus stop.
It is a cold day, and the town is small.
There is a new clock by the sign.
It is noon, and Max is on time.
Zoe and Max are friends.
The bus is at half past six, so they go for a coffee.
dialogue: Hi, Max! It is cold today. What time is it?
Hi, Zoe. Look at the new clock by the sign. It is noon.
Great, we are on time. What time is the bus to the station?
It is at half past six. That is a long way from now.
Really? That is late. What time is the next bus?
The next bus is at two. There is a small schedule on the sign.
Perfect! I would like a hot coffee, please.
Sure, no problem. Two coffees, and then the bus at two.

title: Agendando o jantar
reading: Nora is at home.
There is a calendar on the desk.
Saturday is busy, but Friday is free.
Nora and Lee are friends.
Dinner is on Friday at seven.
It is time for a hot drink!
dialogue: Hi, Lee! Are you free this week? It is time for dinner!
Hmm, my calendar is full. Saturday is busy.
Really? Is Friday free? What is the date?
Friday is free, yes. The date is June twelve.
Perfect! Dinner is on Friday at seven.
Great. Is the place near the station?
Yes, it is. Go straight, and it is by the old sign.
Okay, dinner on Friday. See you there, and I am on time!

title: Um passeio antes do anoitecer
grammar: Before e after antes de um horário ou evento
reading: It is evening, and the sun is low.
The sunset is at seven.
Ella and Sam go for a walk in the park.
The dog is with them.
The evening is cold, so they take a jacket.
After the walk, they read a book and sleep.
dialogue: It is a nice evening, Sam. Please come to the park with me.
Sure! Is the park near your apartment?
Yes, it is. The sunset is at seven, so go before dark.
Good idea. I read a book before dinner, so I am free.
Wonderful. Take a jacket, because the evening is cold.
OK. After dinner I sleep, so I am ready now.
Is it time to go for a walk? Do not run, and stay on the path.
Yes, we are on time. It is before dark. See you at the park!

title: Uma mesa para duas pessoas
grammar: For para indicar para quem ou para quantas pessoas
reading: Chris and Pat are at a restaurant.
It is a busy night.
There is no reservation.
The server is at the desk.
There is a small table by the window.
A menu and some water are on the table.
dialogue: Good evening! Is there a reservation for tonight?
No, there is not. Is there a small table for two?
Yes, there is. Is it a party of two?
Yes, it is. It is Friday at half past six.
Great. Please take the table near the window.
Thank you. Can I have a menu and some water, please?
Sure, here you are. Please speak to me if you need more.
Perfect, thank you. This table for two is nice.

title: Na sala de aula
grammar: Perguntas sobre posse com do e have
reading: It is a new school year.
Omar is in the classroom.
He is at a small desk by the window.
There is a notebook on the desk.
The pencil is not here.
Lia is next to Omar.
dialogue: Hi, Omar! Is this desk free?
Yes, it is. Sit here, next to me.
Thanks. It is a nice classroom.
Yes. What time is the class on Friday?
It is at nine, so we are on time. Oh no, I do not have a pencil!
No problem. I have two pencils. Here you are.
Thank you! Do you have an eraser, too?
Yes, I do. Here you go.

title: Pagando com cartão
grammar: Perguntas de sim ou não com can
reading: I am Leo, and I am at a small store.
My mother and father are at a table by the door.
There is a card reader on the desk.
I have no cash today.
I would like to pay by card.
The receipt is on the desk.
dialogue: Hello! That is eight dollars. Do you have cash or a card?
I do not have cash. Can I pay by card, please?
Yes, you can. Put your card in the card reader.
Okay, here it is. Is the card reader on?
Yes, it is. Please wait a minute.
No problem. Can I have a receipt, too?
Sure. Here is your receipt, and thank you.
Thank you! It is easy to pay by card.

title: Esperando na sala de atendimento
reading: I am in the waiting room.
My sister is with me, and my brother is at work.
I am a patient here, and some people have cash or a card.
There is a sign by the door.
You can wait here, but you cannot run.
The nurse is at the desk.
dialogue: Good morning! Please take a seat in the waiting room.
Thank you. Can I wait here, near the door?
Yes, you can. Please wait, and the doctor is next.
Okay. My sister is in the car. Is there a chair for her, too?
Yes, there is. It is next to the table. Do not run, please.
Sure, no problem. Is there some water here?
Yes, there is water by the desk. But you cannot use a phone here.
Okay, I understand. Thank you!
